evidence.label: Deforming hypersymplectic four-manifolds to hyperkähler triples

headline: Claims every hypersymplectic four-manifold deforms, with its cohomology classes fixed, to a hyperkähler triple.
scope: Smooth hypersymplectic triples of closed two-forms on closed connected oriented four-manifolds.
plain: A hypersymplectic structure is a set of three special two-forms on a four-dimensional space. Hyperkähler triples are the most symmetric such sets. Donaldson asked if every hypersymplectic space carries a hyperkähler structure, and Fine and Yao asked for a deformation that keeps three class labels fixed. Earlier results needed symmetry or other extra conditions. This paper claims a deformation exists in every case, so the space must be a K3 surface or a four-torus.
doesNot: This does not claim the hypersymplectic flow converges; the deformation is built another way. It has no Lean check.
origin: This result comes from an unreleased OpenAI model, published in the openai/math release on 6 October 2026.

scorecard.firstStepBy: Simon Donaldson, Question 3 in his study of two-forms on four-manifolds
scorecard.significanceWhy: It claims a conjecture of Donaldson and of Fine and Yao in four-dimensional geometry, with a strong smooth classification as a corollary.

explanation:
Take the four-torus, a cube in four dimensions whose opposite faces are glued. Use coordinates x1 to x4 and write dxi dxj for a small area element in the xi, xj plane. Form three two-forms: ω1 = dx1 dx2 + dx3 dx4, ω2 = dx1 dx3 + dx4 dx2 and ω3 = dx1 dx4 + dx2 dx3. Multiplying two of them, with the wedge product, gives a multiple of the volume element. Each form times itself gives 2. Each pair of different forms gives 0. So the table of products is 2 times the identity, the same at every point. This is a hyperkähler triple, the most symmetric kind.

Now tilt the third form to ω3 + ω1/2. The table becomes 2, 0, 1 in the first row, 0, 2, 0 in the second and 1, 0, 2.5 in the third. Its eigenvalues are about 3.28, 2 and 1.22, all positive. A triple of closed two-forms whose table is positive like this is hypersymplectic[2]. On a general space the table can change from point to point. A cohomology class is a kind of fixed label for each closed form. The question is whether the forms can move to a hyperkähler triple with their classes kept[2].

Donaldson asked whether every compact four-manifold with such a triple carries a hyperkähler structure[3]. Fine and Yao stated the deformation version, with all three classes fixed, as a conjecture[4]. The main tool so far was the hypersymplectic flow, an equation that moves the forms over time[5]. Full convergence results needed symmetry or other extra conditions[6].

The paper claims the deformation always exists[1]. The endpoint forms are parallel, meaning constant in the right sense, and form a hyperkähler triple[7]. As a result, the space must be smoothly a K3 surface or the four-torus[8]. The obstacle was keeping the third class while deforming. The paper works with two of the forms at a time. Those two forms define an almost-complex structure J, a rule for rotating directions by a right angle. A form tames J if it is positive on each direction paired with its rotation[9]. The deformation works as long as the third class still contains a taming form. To keep one, the paper studies positive currents, which are generalized surfaces that could block the class[10]. It bounds their mass on small balls. It builds on a companion paper that shows taming implies compatibility on four-manifolds[11].

How sure is this? There is no Lean check. A computer proof checker has not looked at any part of it. The proof is long and uses delicate estimates on currents. No specialist review of the paper has been published.
hypeCheck: Major if the proof holds: it would settle a conjecture of Donaldson and of Fine and Yao, and classify such four-manifolds. The proof is long and has no Lean check or published specialist review.

glossary.meaning: A rule that assigns a signed area to each small parallelogram in a space.
A way to multiply two two-forms on a four-dimensional space to get a multiple of the volume element.
Three closed two-forms whose table of wedge products is positive definite at every point.
Three parallel two-forms whose wedge products are 2 times the identity times a volume form.
A label for a closed form that stays fixed under certain allowed changes.
A rule that rotates each tangent direction by a right angle, like multiplying by i.
A two-form tames J if it is positive on each nonzero direction paired with its rotation by J.
A specific compact four-dimensional space, smoothly the same as a smooth quartic surface in complex projective space.
